info.title: Switch Frame Tap
info.author: Papux200
info.description: Stream your games to a PC at 1080p60
info.details:
Switch Frame Tap is a sysmodule that streams the game you are playing - picture and sound - to a Windows, Linux or macOS PC, with no capture card and no dock. It reads the game's finished frames and encodes them with the Switch's own H.264 encoder: native 1080p at 60 fps.

- Play a Switch Lite (or any Switch) on a big screen: a USB cable in handheld, or the network (Wi-Fi or the dock's LAN port) to play docked
- Game audio, also in games that block recording (optional), and recording to MP4 on the PC
- Native-resolution PNG screenshots on a button combo, also next to the system's Album screenshots
- Webcam mode: the Switch shows up as a USB camera, for OBS (H.264, 1080p60) or any camera app (uncompressed, 720p)
- Turn the Switch's screen off while you stream
- This manager app for the settings and to install the optional tools (Ultrahand, SaltyNX, ReverseNX-RT, sys-clk or Horizon OC), plus a Tesla/Ultrahand overlay

Needs Atmosphere (firmware 21 to 23) and the PC viewer (Windows, Linux or macOS) from the GitHub releases page. It reads the running game like a debugger; with cheats loaded for a game it reads through Atmosphere's cheat engine, which is slower.

changelog:
v0.7.14
v0.7.14: the HOME menu and the console's overlays in the stream, a new Switch app, and updates from the apps



- Stream the console's overlays (opt-in).- On the Beta page of the Switch Frame Tap app (or in its overlay), turn on Stream the overlays- and restart. The volume bar, the quick settings (hold HOME), the power menu (hold POWER) and Tesla / Ultrahand menus then show on top of the game, in the viewer and in recordings. They are copied 10-20 times a second, so they move a little less smoothly than the game, and the power menu and 1080p look a bit soft.
- Stream the HOME menu (opt-in).- Stream the HOME menu- shows the HOME menu from boot, System Settings, the user picker, Controllers, My Page, the Album (hold R while opening it) and the Homebrew Menu, and going from a game to the HOME menu and back keeps streaming. No sound outside games yet.
- A new look for the Switch app:- pages on the left (Home, Stream, Picture, Screenshots, Beta, Extras, Setup, Updates, About), the stream's state at a glance, switches for on/off settings. L and R change pages.
- Updates from the apps.- The Switch app's new Updates- page checks GitHub and installs a new version for you (sysmodule, overlay and app - restart the console after). The PC viewers (Windows, Linux, macOS) and the Android app look for a new version when they open and update themselves with one click. Include betas- offers test versions too. From now on, no more zips by hand.
- The Android / Android TV app- (by didix16) is part of the release: switch-frame-tap-0.7.14-android.apk, for Android TV, Google TV, phones and tablets (Android 6+), over the network or USB. Install it with a file manager that can install apps.
- Fixes:- opening the eShop from the HOME menu while streaming works again (firmware 22 and later). A failed engine setup no longer needs a reboot. Shorter gaps going from the HOME menu into a game. Should fix the stream not coming back in Pokémon Violet after a drop (20). The Android app replaces a decoder that drops most frames (should fix 1 fps on Chromecast 4K, 27).
- Viewers:- a new borderless Windows viewer window with responsive settings, and network streams that show a picture right away when the viewer joins mid-game (both by bshurikan). The viewers explain USB-C to USB-C cable trouble. A PC without a working GPU driver gets a picture (drawn in software) instead of an error.

Both betas are off by default. With them off it streams like v0.7.13.2 (same frame rate and timings side by side); the sysmodule needs about 0.1 MB more system memory.

Installing:- unzip switch-frame-tap-0.7.14-switch.zip over the SD card root and reboot (settings are kept), and install the new viewer. Next time, the apps can do it for you.


Switch Frame Tap is free and open source. If you would like to support it: buymeacoffee.com/papux200: https://buymeacoffee.com/papux200

0.7.13.1: streaming no longer stops until a reboot after closing some homebrew apps (Sphaira, for example).
0.7.13: fixes a black screen after launching many apps in a row, and the boot crash on consoles with several sysmodules (it now starts about 30 s after boot, only if there is enough memory); uses about half the system memory; Super Mario Odyssey fills the stream; smoother over Wi-Fi.
0.7.12: new PC viewer design (one Settings panel), picture controls and a recording timer; turn the Switch's screen off while streaming; a few ms less latency at 1080p.
0.7.11: firmware 23.0 / Atmosphere 1.12; macOS viewer; pressing HOME while streaming no longer crashes manuals or the eShop; screenshots next to the system's, and a custom combo with the Capture button; GPU upscaling in the viewer.
0.7.10: game manuals, news and the eShop work with Switch Frame Tap installed (it holds no applet memory while not streaming).
0.7.9: streaming while cheats are loaded (through Atmosphere's cheat engine); Xenoblade Chronicles X and Fire Emblem: Three Houses fixes.
0.7.8: back to 720p at once when leaving docked mode, also in 30 fps games; firmware 21.x streams by default.
0.7.7: a webcam for any camera app; no more fatal on Atmosphere older than 1.11.2.
0.7.6: no zoom on fake-docked menu changes.
0.7.5: install the optional tools from the manager.
0.7.4: sound in games that block recording, built in.
